questions.q: In a stage's Summary Metrics, what signals skew?

options.t: More tasks than shuffle partitions
A minimum task duration of zero seconds
Spill reported on every task in the stage, whatever the durations
A max task duration 50% or more above the 75th percentile

questions.explain: Databricks' guide: skew shows as a max task duration 50% or more above the 75th percentile.

questions.q: A groupBy on seller is skewed by one seller. AQE is on. Why does the stage stay slow?

options.t: AQE splits skewed partitions in joins, not in aggregations
AQE never touches stages with more than 200 partitions
AQE only coalesces small partitions; it never splits large ones in any operation
options.why: It does split skewed join partitions.

options.t: AQE is off by default and must be enabled

questions.explain: AQE splits skewed partitions in sort-merge and shuffle-hash joins; a skewed aggregation needs salting and a two-stage aggregation.

questions.q: Which fix spreads a skewed aggregation's hot key over many tasks?

options.t: Add more workers so the hot key's task gets more memory
options.why: The hot key still goes to one task.

options.t: Salt the hot key and aggregate in two stages
Cache the DataFrame before grouping
Raise spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold

questions.explain: Salting the hot key and aggregating in two stages spreads it; other fixes from the guide include liquid clustering for skewed stored tables and the REBALANCE hint for skewed output.

questions.q: A stage spills heavily during a shuffle. Which change does Databricks' guide suggest first?

options.t: Increase the trigger interval so each batch has more time
options.why: Only for streams, and not the first step.

options.t: Disable AQE
options.why: AQE helps; disabling it doesn't fix spill.

options.t: `spark.sql.shuffle.partitions=auto`
Turn off Photon

questions.explain: For spill the guide suggests shuffle.partitions=auto, fewer rows or columns, more executor memory, fewer larger workers for complex joins, and smaller streaming batches.

questions.q: Which of these does AQE do at run time? (Choose two.)

options.t: Switch a sort-merge join to a broadcast hash join when one side turns out small
Coalesce small post-shuffle partitions
Rewrite a streaming query's plan between micro-batches
options.why: AQE doesn't apply to streaming queries.

options.t: Split skewed partitions in a groupBy aggregation
options.why: Its skew handling is for joins.

options.t: Add Z-order to the source table

questions.explain: At each shuffle or broadcast exchange AQE uses real statistics to switch joins to broadcast, coalesce small partitions, split skewed join partitions and propagate empty relations.

questions.q: What is the Apache Spark default for spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold?

options.t: 1 MB
100 MB
-1, so broadcasting is off by default
options.why: -1 disables it; the default is 10 MB.

options.t: 10 MB

questions.explain: The largest table broadcast to every worker for a join, 10 MB by default in Apache Spark; -1 disables broadcasting. Databricks Runtime can set its own defaults.

questions.q: What does Databricks recommend for the layout of all new tables?

options.t: Liquid clustering
No layout at all; predictive optimization picks partitions
Bucketing by the join key
Partitioning by date, plus Z-order on the filter column

questions.explain: Liquid clustering replaces partitioning and ZORDER, its keys can change without rewriting data, and Databricks recommends it for all new tables.

questions.q: `CLUSTER BY AUTO` is set on a table. What does it need?

options.t: Z-order on the same columns
A Unity Catalog managed table with predictive optimization
An external Delta table on Databricks Runtime 13.3 LTS or above
options.why: Automatic clustering is for managed tables.

options.t: A partitioned table
options.why: Liquid clustering isn't compatible with partitioning.

questions.explain: Automatic liquid clustering needs predictive optimization on a UC managed table; Databricks picks keys from query history, and may pick none.

questions.q: Clustering keys must change. What happens to existing data?

options.t: Old files are deleted
It is rewritten immediately with the new keys, which can take hours on a large table
options.why: Changing keys doesn't rewrite old data.

options.t: Nothing at once; OPTIMIZE clusters new data, and OPTIMIZE FULL reclusters everything
The table must be recreated
options.why: ALTER TABLE CLUSTER BY changes keys.

questions.explain: Clustering is incremental; changing keys doesn't rewrite existing data; OPTIMIZE t FULL reclusters all of it.

questions.q: What does predictive optimization run, and on which tables?

options.t: OPTIMIZE with ZORDER BY on the most-queried columns, on every table in the metastore
VACUUM only, on external tables
options.why: It works on managed tables, and runs more than VACUUM.

options.t: Schema evolution, on streaming tables
OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE, on Unity Catalog managed tables

questions.explain: Predictive optimization runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE on UC managed tables only, on serverless jobs compute; its OPTIMIZE never runs ZORDER.

questions.q: deletedFileRetentionDuration is 2 days on a table maintained by predictive optimization. How long are removed files kept?

options.t: At least 7 days
2 days
30 days
Until someone runs VACUUM by hand

questions.explain: Its VACUUM honours the property but keeps at least 7 days even if the property is lower.

questions.q: Why enable deletion vectors on a table with frequent small UPDATEs?

options.t: They make reads faster by deleting old files at once
options.why: They mark rows; readers apply the marks.

options.t: DML marks changed rows instead of rewriting whole files
They let the table be read by any Delta client, including older ones
options.why: Enabling them upgrades the protocol, which some clients can't read.

options.t: They replace VACUUM

questions.explain: Deletion vectors speed up DELETE, UPDATE and MERGE by marking rows in metadata; enabling them upgrades the protocol.

questions.q: What is the disk cache?

options.t: A SQL warehouse result cache
options.why: That is the query result cache.

options.t: A Delta Lake feature that caches the transaction log
options.why: It is a Databricks feature for Parquet files.

options.t: Workers' local copies of Parquet files read from cloud storage, so repeated reads are faster
The Spark cache under another name, filled by calling df.cache() on each DataFrame
options.why: Databricks recommends it over the Spark cache.

questions.explain: The disk cache (formerly the Delta cache) keeps local copies of Parquet files on workers; it is automatic on supported worker types.

questions.q: A nightly serverless job can start a few minutes late without harm. Which performance setting saves cost?

options.t: A classic all-purpose cluster kept running
Autoscaling turned off on the serverless task
Performance optimized, which uses a cheaper SKU because it finishes sooner
options.why: Both modes use the same SKU.

options.t: Standard performance mode (Performance optimized off), which uses fewer DBUs

questions.explain: Standard performance mode uses less compute, tolerating startup latency of 4 to 6 minutes; both modes bill the same SKU, standard consuming fewer DBUs.

questions.q: What does Databricks recommend for the compute of job tasks?

options.t: Serverless compute
SQL warehouses for Python tasks
options.why: Python tasks don't run on SQL warehouses.

options.t: All-purpose clusters, shared by every job
A dedicated classic cluster per task

questions.explain: The serverless jobs page: Databricks recommends using serverless compute for all job tasks.

questions.q: On Azure, what counts as Jobs Compute for billing?

options.t: Any notebook run by a service principal
A job that both starts and terminates the cluster it runs on
Any job at all, on any cluster, including all-purpose clusters it shares
options.why: Jobs on all-purpose clusters are all-purpose workloads.

options.t: Any cluster with auto termination

questions.explain: The pricing page defines Jobs Compute as a job that both starts and terminates its cluster, billed at a different rate from all-purpose compute.

questions.q: Which statements about pools are correct? (Choose two.)

options.t: They keep idle instances ready to cut start-up and autoscaling time
No DBUs are charged for idle pool instances, though the cloud bills the VMs
Databricks recommends pools over serverless
Idle pool instances are free of all charges
options.why: The cloud provider still bills the VMs.

options.t: Pools are only for SQL warehouses

questions.explain: Pools keep idle instances to cut start-up and autoscaling time; idle pool instances incur no DBUs, but the VMs are billed by the cloud; Databricks recommends serverless where possible.

questions.q: Which levers lower cost for classic compute? (Choose two.)

options.t: Automatic termination after idle minutes
Spot instances for workers where latency allows
Running scheduled jobs on all-purpose clusters
options.why: Job compute is billed differently and recommended for automated work.

options.t: Spot instances for the driver
Turning Photon off for every workload

questions.explain: Cost levers include auto termination, spot workers, smaller instances for simple ETL, job compute for automated work, serverless or pools, and policies.

questions.q: What is Photon?

options.t: A file format replacing Parquet
A cache for query results
A native vectorized engine that speeds up SQL, DataFrames and Delta writes without code changes
A streaming trigger for sub-second latency on operational workloads

questions.explain: Photon is a native C++ vectorized engine, enabled by default from DBR 9.1 LTS, that speeds up SQL, DataFrames, ETL and Delta writes.

questions.q: Many analysts run ad hoc SQL at unpredictable times. Which warehouse type does Databricks favour?

options.t: An all-purpose cluster with a SQL endpoint
Classic, for the lowest unit price
Pro, because it runs in your cloud account
options.why: Pro is for when serverless isn't available or custom networking is needed.

options.t: Serverless

questions.explain: Serverless SQL warehouses start in seconds and scale fast with Intelligent Workload Management: Databricks' choice for many concurrent BI and ad hoc users.

questions.q: Which statements about OPTIMIZE (bin-packing) are correct? (Choose two.)

options.t: It makes no data change, so readers and streams are unaffected
A second run on the same data does nothing: it is idempotent
It deletes the old files immediately
It balances files by row count
options.why: Bin-packing balances by size; Z-order by row count.

options.t: It requires ZORDER BY
options.why: ZORDER is optional, and not for liquid-clustered tables.

questions.explain: OPTIMIZE rewrites small files into larger ones with no data change; bin-packing is idempotent and balances by size.

questions.q: On which columns does Delta collect data-skipping statistics by default?

options.t: The first 32 columns
None until ANALYZE runs
All columns
Only clustering keys

questions.explain: Statistics (min, max, null count, record count per file) are collected on write for the first 32 columns by default (delta.dataSkippingNumIndexedCols).

questions.q: A stateful streaming query's spark.sql.shuffle.partitions is raised after it started. What happens?

options.t: New partitions take effect at the next micro-batch, and state is spread across them
options.why: Shuffle partitions are fixed when the checkpoint is created.

options.t: No effect on that query: the count is fixed when the checkpoint is created
The query fails at once
options.why: It doesn't fail; the setting is ignored for it.

options.t: State is redistributed automatically on DBR 11.3

questions.explain: Shuffle partitions are fixed when a stateful query's checkpoint is created; DBR 18 LTS+ can repartition stateful queries on demand.

questions.q: Which state store does Databricks recommend for stateful streaming?

options.t: Redis on the driver
The in-memory HDFS-backed store
RocksDB with changelog checkpointing
A Delta table updated in foreachBatch

questions.explain: RocksDB is the default from DBR 17.3; Databricks recommends it with changelog checkpointing. The state store type can't change between restarts without a new checkpoint.

questions.q: Which advice applies to Structured Streaming jobs in production?

options.t: Turn on autoscaling so the cluster follows the input rate
options.why: Databricks advises against autoscaling for streaming jobs.

options.t: Keep display() calls for debugging
Call awaitTermination() so the job waits
options.why: Not in jobs: it blocks tracking.

options.t: Run them on jobs compute, scheduled in Continuous mode

questions.explain: Run production streams as jobs or pipelines on jobs compute, scheduled in Continuous mode; don't autoscale; remove display and count; don't call awaitTermination() in jobs.

questions.q: Finance wants DBU spend per team. Which combination gives it?

options.t: Compute tags, which flow to usage records, with system.billing.usage
The Spark UI's executor page
DESCRIBE HISTORY on every table
Query history's duration column, multiplied by each warehouse's size

questions.explain: Tags on compute flow to usage logs for attribution; system.billing.usage holds usage, joined with list prices for cost.

questions.q: VACUUM is slow on a large table. What does the VACUUM page say about sizing?

options.t: Size doesn't matter; it is metadata-only
Listing uses the workers; deleting is driver-only
Everything runs on the driver, so adding workers can't help at all
It runs only on serverless

questions.explain: Listing uses the workers and deleting is driver-only; the page suggests autoscaling 1-4 workers of 8 cores and a driver of 8-32 cores. LITE mode uses the log instead of listing.
